ruxen 0.2.3: a way to try ruxen on real traffic behind nginx (shadow mode, differential testing, Prometheus metrics, a migration guide), every proxied response relayed with nginx's buffering, HTTP/2 and DNS-discovered upstreams with session affinity, `aio threads`, kTLS, and many fixes found by comparing answers with nginx 1.30.6. ruxen is an experimental nginx-compatible HTTP server and reverse proxy written from scratch in Rust: Linux-only, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, thread-per-core on `io_uring` (monoio, epoll where `io_uring` is blocked), TLS via rustls.

> [!WARNING]
> This is an experimental release. It is not production-ready and is not a drop-in replacement for nginx.

**Try ruxen without risk**, the first part of the next phase in `ROADMAP.md`, which now puts a first user before completeness (#753). **Shadow mode** (#754, [`docs/shadow.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.3/docs/shadow.md)): nginx stays in front and answers every request, its `mirror` sends each `GET` and `HEAD` to ruxen running the site's configuration on other ports, and `scripts/shadow-report.py` joins the two access logs by `$request_id` and reports where the answers differ, as Markdown for an issue. **Metrics**: `ruxen_metrics;` in a location answers in Prometheus text format, with the `stub_status` counters, responses and bytes per server, requests, failures, response times and state per upstream peer, and requests per `limit_req`, `limit_conn` and cache zone (#768, #787, #880, [`docs/metrics.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.3/docs/metrics.md)). **A migration guide** ([`docs/migrating.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.3/docs/migrating.md), #770) takes each `--compat` finding in turn: what ruxen does instead, when it matters, what to do and the issue that tracks it; `--compat` links the section for each finding. **Differential testing** (#790): `scripts/difftest/` sends the same configurations and requests to nginx 1.30.6 and to ruxen and reports where the answers differ. Its first run compared 374 configurations and 103,615 requests; most of the fixes below come from it.

**Every proxied response is relayed as it arrives** (#463): a response stored in `proxy_cache`, one an `error_page`, `proxy_intercept_errors`, `proxy_next_upstream` or X-Accel-Redirect handles, a `Range` request under `proxy_cache` or `proxy_force_ranges`, and one with `add_trailer` (#767, #791, #794, #821). Before, these were read whole first, and a body over 64 MiB was a 502. **`proxy_buffering` works as nginx's** (#834): with a slow client, ruxen keeps reading the upstream into `proxy_buffers`, then into a temp file up to `proxy_max_temp_file_size`, and the upstream connection goes back to the pool once the body is in. Before, the upstream waited on the client. **`proxy_request_buffering off`** streams the request body to the upstream (#861). With these, every `proxy_cache*.t` of nginx-tests that runs without SSI passes, and the proxy cache tracking issue is closed (#233). Upstreams also gained nginx 1.27–1.29's `proxy_http_version 2`, `server … resolve` and `sticky` (see nginx compatibility).

## Performance

Against 0.2.2 on the headline scenarios (i7, 6 ABBA pairs each): `proxy_64k` 137.3%, `h2_tls_hello` 103.7%, `h2c_hello` 102.3%, `m1_hello` 100.5%, `tls_hello` 100.0%, `m3_static_1k` 99.7%, `gzip_html_8k` 99.5%, `proxy_hello` 98.2%. The `proxy_hello` loss adds up from several correctness changes on the proxy path, each within about 1% in its own ABBA.

- **Large proxied bodies on `io_uring`** (#842): the relay and the request body read the socket at once (`recv`) instead of through the ring: a ring read copies the bytes while the kernel works through every connection's completions, and by the time they were written on they had left the cache. `proxy_1m` +63.3%, `proxy_ext_1m` (nginx backend) +75.6%, `proxy_64k` +31.6%, `proxy_post_64k` +31.7% (i7, 6 ABBA pairs each). Against nginx 1.30.6 on the i7, `proxy_1m` went from 96.5% to 157.3%. A response to a request whose body was read goes out at once too (#856): `proxy_post_64k` +11.6% more. It was at 69.6% of nginx in the 0.2.1 campaign and 88.6% after #842 (#289).
- **Proxying without upstream keep-alive** (#862): ruxen closes an unpooled upstream connection after the upstream closes its end, so the TIME_WAIT sockets stay on the backend's side. Under `io_uring`, ruxen often closed first and filled its ephemeral ports. `proxy_no_upstream_keepalive` +22.7% (i7, 6 pairs).
- **`io_uring` rings with `SINGLE_ISSUER | DEFER_TASKRUN`** (#755): the kernel no longer interrupts a worker for each completion. `m1_hello` +1.5%, `proxy_hello` +2.4%, `m1_hello_c4096` +3.3%, `static_8k` +1.6% (i7, 6 pairs). Kernels before 6.1 get the rings without them.
- **Keep-alive requests of different sizes** (#723): after a short request, a longer next head on the connection came in pieces of the short one's length, up to 8 reads. The new `m1_varied_heads` scenario (#729) sends heads of about 40, 300, 1300 and 2700 bytes in turn: +35.0% (i7, 6 pairs).
- **Memory per idle keep-alive connection** (#725, #843): about 4.8 KB, down from 12.5 KB after a `return 200` and 24.9 KB after an 8 KiB static file (i9; nginx 1.30.6: 0.6 KB). The request's state is freed between requests, as nginx frees it, and `client_header_buffer_size` (1k) now sizes the first read. `static_8k_c4096` +2.8%, `m1_hello` −0.5% (i9, 6 pairs).
- **The cost of `proxy_buffering`** (#834): buffering for a slow client takes about 2–3% off `proxy_1m` (97.2% and 97.8% in two ABBA runs on the i7, 6 pairs each), accepted for nginx's behaviour.

## Security

ruxen has no known production users yet; these were found by differential testing against nginx 1.30.6 and by review, and fixed in the open. Upgrade from 0.2.2.

- **A regex location nested in a prefix location matched every URI** (#730, #731): nested locations were flattened into the server's list, so a server-level regex rule after one (`deny`, `return 403`) was skipped, and one before it shadowed it and its prefix location's `auth_basic`. Locations are now searched level by level, as nginx's `ngx_http_core_find_location`. Random location trees up to three levels deep now get the same answers as from nginx 1.30.6 (135 configurations, 40 URIs each).
- **Regexes didn't match bytes that aren't UTF-8** (#797, #805): `location ~ ^/private/.*$ { deny all; }` let `/private/%FF` through to `location /`. Every regex is now byte-oriented, as nginx's PCRE without UTF: `.` and negated classes match any byte, `\w`, `\d` and caseless matching are ASCII.
- **An open redirect through `rewrite`** (#798, #817): a replacement starting with a capture redirected to whatever URL the request carried (`rewrite ^/v/(.*)$ $1;` and `/v/http://evil.example/`). Whether a rewrite redirects is now decided on the replacement as written, as in nginx.
- **The request body was read before the access checks** (#855, #863): `auth_basic`, `allow` / `deny`, `auth_request`, `limit_req` and `limit_conn` answered only after ruxen had read and stored the whole upload, up to `client_max_body_size`. They now answer first and the body is discarded, as nginx's access phase does.
- **`autoindex_format jsonp` reflected any callback as script** (#833, #803). The callback is checked as nginx checks it (at most 128 bytes of `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, else 400), and the answer is `application/javascript`.
- **tokio 1.54.1** (RUSTSEC-2026-0386, #722): `AsyncFd::new` and related constructors were unsound. ruxen never builds an `AsyncFd`, so it wasn't affected; the lock moves to the fixed release.

## Fixes

- **A request with a body is answered without waiting for it** wherever nginx does (rest of #627): a server-level `return` (the http→https redirect server), a `try_files` that finds a file or answers `=code`, and the 400 for a target that doesn't normalise (#840, #869). A malformed chunked body gets its location's 400, with its `error_page` and `add_header … always`, and the connection closes (#870); a chunked body nobody reads is parsed, so a request pipelined behind it is served (#740). No `100 Continue` goes out before an error for a body nobody reads (#739). A body that stops coming or whose client leaves closes the connection unanswered, with 408 or 400 in the access log, as nginx logs it (#865, #871).
- **`listen … default_server` picked nothing for plain HTTP** (#732): a request with an unknown or missing `Host` went to the first server of the address, not to the catch-all `default_server` block.
- **`try_files $uri @app` answered PUT, DELETE, PATCH and OPTIONS with 405** (#733) before the fallback ran, so a REST API behind it never saw them. The 405 is the static module's again: only for what is served from disk.
- **Idle keep-alive connections never closed without `keepalive_timeout`** (#773, #816). They now close after nginx's 75 s default. An HTTP/2 connection that sends no stream is bounded by `client_header_timeout`, as in nginx, not by `keepalive_timeout`.
- **The SPA pattern `try_files $uri =404; error_page 404 /index.html;`** answered a conditional request with a 404 without a body or `Content-Length`, and a `Range` request with a piece of the page (#718). The page now goes whole under a 404, and under `=200` its 304 and 206 stay.
- **A `HEAD` sent upstream as another method** (`proxy_method`) got the upstream's body after the header, which broke keep-alive (#741).
- **The two halves of a tunnel or an HTTP/2 connection held two `&mut` to one stream** (#501, #792): undefined behaviour, which Miri confirmed. They are now separate read and write halves.
- **A cache hit with `add_trailer` was read into memory** (#793, #821): a 48 MiB entry took the worker to 204 MB. It is sent from the cache file.
- **A far-range request under `proxy_cache_lock` kept the lock** until `proxy_cache_lock_age`, so every request for the key waited (#864, #867).
- `listen … reuseport` alone didn't let another process share the address; it took another socket option with it (#761, #795).

## nginx compatibility

- **Upstreams:**
  - **`proxy_http_version 2`** (nginx 1.29.4, #599, #824): h2c by prior knowledge for `http://`, ALPN `h2` for `https://`, one stream at a time per connection, kept with `keepalive`. Buffering, relay, `proxy_next_upstream` and the cache are shared with HTTP/1.1.
  - **`server NAME resolve`** and `service=` (SRV records) in an upstream with a `zone` (nginx 1.27.3, #597, #804, #827): the peers follow the DNS answers at run time, with `resolver` inside `upstream {}`. A reload starts from the last answers.
  - **`sticky cookie | route | learn`**, `server … route=` and `drain` (nginx 1.29.6, #600, #822, #887), also with `resolve` servers. Peer IDs are computed as nginx computes them, so the cookies match nginx's.
  - **`proxy_pass_trailers`** (nginx 1.27.2, #845), for HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 upstreams.
  - **`early_hints`** (nginx 1.29.0, #857): an upstream's 103 Early Hints reaches the client while the final response is awaited, as an informational HEADERS frame on HTTP/2.
- **TLS:**
  - **`ssl_ocsp`, `ssl_ocsp_responder` and `ssl_ocsp_cache`** (#142, #819): client certificates are checked with OCSP before the first request, resumed sessions too. A revoked one is a 495 (sent as 400), with nginx's `$ssl_client_verify` values.
  - **Kernel TLS** with `ssl_conf_command Options KTLS` (#673, #854, #875): after the handshake the kernel encrypts and decrypts, and `sendfile on` sends files over TLS without a copy. It needs the `tls` kernel module; without it ruxen warns and stays in userspace. TLS 1.3 key updates work where the kernel can rekey (6.14+). Not measured against nginx's kTLS yet (#853).
  - **`ssl_ciphers`** is applied with OpenSSL's rules over the six TLS 1.2 suites rustls has, and `ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on` takes the server's order (#726). certbot's and Mozilla's snippets load without a warning.
  - `proxy_ssl_certificate_cache` (nginx 1.27.4, #788).
- **Static files:**
  - **Variables and captures in `root` and `alias`** (#232, #765), refused at startup until now. Stricter than nginx: a `..` or NUL that a variable brings into the path is a 403.
  - **`gzip_static on | always`** serves `file.gz` (#760, #810).
  - **`aio threads` and `thread_pool`** (#526, #820, #860): file reads, `sendfile` and `proxy_cache` entry reads run on a thread pool, so a slow disk stalls a pool thread instead of the worker. With a FUSE file whose reads take 3 s, another request to the same worker waited 2.7 s without it and 0.3 ms with it.
  - **`etag on | off`** and **`if_modified_since off | exact | before`** (#734, #744). The default `exact` no longer answers 304 to a later date, and the preconditions are evaluated in nginx's order.
  - Several ranges are sent from the file whatever their size, as `multipart/byteranges`; over 1 MiB, ruxen sent the whole file (#414, #812).
  - `add_trailer` on a file of any size: the response goes chunked, as in nginx (#844, #872).
  - `return`, autoindex and `stub_status` 200s answer `If-Match`, `If-Unmodified-Since` and `If-None-Match: *` (#782, #813).
  - With `gzip_vary`, a 206 or 416 of a file gzip would take carries `Vary` (#719, #745).
  - autoindex JSON, JSONP and XML bodies are nginx's byte for byte (#802, #851).
  - An external request to an `internal` location gets its `error_page` for the 404 (#746); a missing index directory is logged with the index file's name (#796).
- **Requests:**
  - the request line is parsed as nginx parses it: extra spaces, `HTTP/1.2`–`HTTP/1.99` as 1.1, 505 for `HTTP/2.0` and above (#747); empty lines before it are skipped, and HTTP/0.9 is a 400 at once (#815);
  - a bad request line is refused before a bad header (#868); a URI above the root (`/../x`) is a 400 that closes the connection (#717); so is an HTTP/1.1 absolute-form request without `Host` (#829);
  - a request refused before routing gets the default server's `add_header … always` and `error_page`, no body for `HEAD`, and a lingering close instead of a reset (#818);
  - the connection closes after nginx's own 400, 413, 414, 495–497, 500 and 501, and `return 494`–`497` sends nginx's 400 page (#742);
  - `$request_uri` keeps a `#fragment`, and so does the target `proxy_pass` sends without a URI part (#772, #799);
  - `auth_basic` decodes credentials as nginx (stray padding, `Basic` and a space) (#743);
  - realip walks several `X-Forwarded-For` lines one by one, from the last (#786, #828).
- **Rewrite, map and try_files:**
  - a `rewrite` target is rendered as nginx's script code: escaped captures keep an encoded `%` and `#` (`50%25-off` became `50-off`), the arguments and an empty URI as in nginx (#735, #762, #766);
  - `map` regex captures in values (`$1`, named groups), and a matching map regex sets the request's captures (#800, #832, #838);
  - a `{` that starts no quantifier is a literal, as in PCRE2 (#763, #801);
  - a `try_files` fallback URI without `?` has no arguments (#811, #849);
  - a named location (`try_files … @app`, `error_page … @app`, also after `proxy_intercept_errors`) sends the upstream the client's request target and keeps a `rewrite`'s URI (#777, #814, #825, #850).
- **Proxy cache:** `proxy_no_cache` is tested once the upstream's header is in, so `$upstream_http_*` works there (#826, #846); with `proxy_cache_convert_head off` a HEAD's answer is stored (#837); the cache manager follows `manager_files`, `manager_sleep`, `manager_threshold` and the zone's watermark (#839, #847).
- **gzip:** `gzip_types *` takes a response without `Content-Type` (#808, #830); a handler's response with `add_trailer` is compressed (#809, #874).
- **Configuration:**
  - `keepalive_min_timeout` (nginx 1.27.4, #788) and `client_header_buffer_size` (#725) are applied;
  - `http3` and the `quic_*` directives load, reported as differs (no HTTP/3) (#720);
  - `connection_pool_size`, `request_pool_size` and `large_client_header_buffers` are checked as nginx checks them (#749);
  - nginx's messages for a missing `;` or `{` and for an upstream host that doesn't resolve (#728);
  - `server_name *.example.com` no longer matches `example.com` itself, for `Host` and SNI (#737);
  - an `alias` whose location and path disagree on a trailing `/` gets a warning: nginx maps such a pair outside the directory, ruxen doesn't (#736).
- `-V` claims `--with-http_gzip_static_module` and `--with-threads`, and no longer `--without-http_upstream_sticky_module`.

## Operations

- **CLI** (#721): `-h`, `--help` and `--version`; without `-c` the configuration is `/etc/ruxen/ruxen.conf`, the path the systemd unit and the images use; a missing configuration is reported in nginx's words.
- **`--compat`** (#727, #770): repeated findings on one line, the module ruxen lacks named (FastCGI, uwsgi, …), warnings with their place, and a link to the guide's section for each kind of finding.
- **Reloads under `user`** (#344, #775, #831): a reload binds new ports below 1024, with `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` kept as the only capability. At startup ruxen warns about each file the configuration reads that `user` can't, since a reload would fail on it (#774).
- **Packaging:** the tarballs ship `contrib/`: the systemd unit, the logrotate snippet and the seccomp profile (#554, #758).
- **Fuzzing** (#477, #789): `h2_request`, `rewrite` and `realip` targets, each against a model of nginx's behaviour (the `rewrite` target found #762). Long runs happen nightly on a private machine, and `scripts/fuzz_long.sh --report` sums their hours for a release.
- **Benchmarks on other hardware** (#14, #759): a manual workflow runs ruxen against nginx 1.30.6 on GitHub's hosted x86_64 and ARM64 runners. Its first run: 113–143% of nginx on the keep-alive scenarios, 96.3% (x86_64) and 92.4% (ARM64) on `m1_no_keepalive`.

## Install

Three prebuilt binaries, each also under a versioned name (`ruxen-v0.2.3-<target>.tar.gz`), with a `SHA256SUMS` file:

| tarball | for |
| --- | --- |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer |
| `ruxen-aarch64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | ARM64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Graviton, Ampere, Raspberry Pi 5 on a 64-bit OS) |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any x86_64 Linux, static (Alpine, older glibc) |

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/releases/download/v0.2.3/ruxen-v0.2.3-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS   # after downloading SHA256SUMS from this release
tar xzf ruxen-v0.2.3-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
cd ruxen-v0.2.3-x86_64-linux-gnu
./ruxen -t -c "$PWD/examples/minimal.conf"
```

Container image, amd64 and arm64:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/gvozdetsky/ruxen:0.2.3
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/
```

It runs as an unprivileged user. Docker's default seccomp profile blocks `io_uring`, so under it ruxen runs on epoll; [`contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.3/contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json) allows `io_uring` and nothing else beyond the default (`--security-opt seccomp=contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`). On a host with many cores, the container's memlock limit may need raising for `io_uring` (`--ulimit memlock=134217728`, #612); without it the workers that don't fit run on epoll (#635). A hardened systemd unit and a logrotate snippet are in [`contrib/`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/tree/v0.2.3/contrib) and in the tarballs.

From crates.io (needs `cmake` and a C compiler for rustls's `aws-lc-rs` backend):

```bash
cargo install ruxen --locked
```

## Tests

nginx-tests: 212 of the 223 files ruxen opts into pass (0.2.2: 182 of 197), see [`NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.3/NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md). Config corpus: ruxen loads 220 of 238 real-world configurations (92%; 0.2.2: 218), 210 of them with nothing that behaves differently from nginx (0.2.2: 171).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/compare/v0.2.2...v0.2.3
